rule: A Ralph park citing `iteration ended without a pushed branch` may be loop infrastructure rather than the issue's work — check the claude-step outcome and the agent's own comment before believing the issue is stuck.
rationale: ops#44's two attempt-failures were claude-code-action rejecting bot-actor pushes, fixed in #119/#120; the issue was fine. Signal appeared independently on #39 and #240 too.

rule: Before re-queuing a previously blocked or parked issue, read its comment history — `closed_by_pull_requests` plus the current code is not sufficient evidence the blocker is gone.
rationale: ops#142 was re-queued by a 2026-09-14 burndown sweep that checked only closed PRs and code; it burned a full iteration rediscovering a blocker recorded in July. Adrian's own follow-up generalised the rule.

rule: When a gate fails citing a missing binary or dependency, install it and re-run before trusting that diagnosis — the real fault can be a stale config or an architectural mismatch underneath.
rationale: ops#178 parked blaming a missing Playwright Chromium binary; with Chromium installed the real faults were a stale DEFAULT_ROUTES list and a gate architecturally unable to test /ops/* (vite preview doesn't run the serverless gate API).

rule: A `ralph-gate` startup_failure with zero jobs run means caller/reusable permission or version skew on a stale branch — update the branch from `main` before concluding the shared engine regressed.
rationale: ops#144 root-caused the #133 outage: the engine's gate job began requesting actions:write, which a reusable can never exceed its caller's grant for; only pre-ops#132 branches lacked it.

rule: Before executing a deletion or cleanup issue, diff its stated premise against current `main` — a prior unrelated PR may have solved the problem differently, making the literal DoD stale. Stop and ask rather than deleting working code on the issue text's word.
rationale: ops#122's target dead code no longer existed as described; PR #124 had rescoped the suites a different way. The deletion was still wanted, but only a human could confirm that.

rule: Before tagging an issue ralph-ready, confirm the file or script it targets actually exists in this repo — stale board imports point at other repos.
rationale: ops#63 targeted scripts/check-typography-discipline.mjs, which has no history in ops; the stack trace pointed at the separate portfolio repo, already flagged do-not-re-file.

rule: Backlog items describing pre-extraction design-system structure (HDS pages, /hds routes) are suspect — ops consumes @hirobius/design-system and no longer authors or hosts it.
rationale: ops#70 wanted HDS doc pages absorbed into /ops/atlas; those pages had been moved out to the standalone design-system repo entirely.

rule: Before treating a `ralph-blocked: fix is in an open unmerged PR` as resolved, verify that PR's mergeable_state — a stale or conflicting branch stalls the whole queue under single-flight and must be closed and re-dispatched, not waited on.
rationale: ops#233's PR #235 went stale and conflicted with main after #244; a human closed it and re-dispatched, landing as #246.

rule: An issue whose DoD requires editing `.github/workflows/*` must be split before queueing: the workflow file goes to a human or an adr-eng PR, the rest is re-filed as a script/registry-only issue Ralph can push.
rationale: The bot's token lacks the workflows scope. ops#90, #240, #241 and #243 each independently did the full work and then died at the push — four issues rediscovering the same documented wall.

rule: A pre-commit gate must not hard-fail the hook on a warn-severity finding, and a pre-commit failure should be checked for reproducibility on `main` before being treated as this issue's fault.
rationale: ops#262: check-validator-wiring's substring matcher read a prose mention of 'audit-sbom' in a quality.yml comment as live wiring, emitting a warn-severity WIRING_DRIFT. run-gates.mjs/husky fail on any non-zero exit regardless of severity, so a false positive blocked every commit repo-wide.

rule: The harness park comment must echo the agent's own `ralph-blocked` reason rather than substituting a generic diagnosis — a mismatched park reason hides the true state from whoever reviews it.
rationale: ops#103's park said 'branch pushed but PR creation failed after 3 attempts (auth/network?)'. The agent had just correctly reported the issue was already shipped in merged PR #192 and no push had failed.

rule: A PR body's `Closes #N` is not proof the issue will auto-close — verify the transition after merge and close directly if it didn't, or the loop re-claims finished work indefinitely.
rationale: ops#156 accumulated 12+ ralph-blocked re-claims over ~12 hours on already-shipped work; ops#103, #3, #205, #210 and #282 show the same pattern.

rule: Treat a `ralph-blocked` comment that does not result in the issue actually being parked within one cycle as a harness defect to fix, not a reason to re-dispatch.
rationale: ops#156: 5+ blocked comments accumulated before parking stuck. The agent named the likely cause itself — reconcile_issue's blocked-parking path.
